January 1960

Wednesday, Jan. 6
  1. In Laos · Laos, By Jan. 6An army communiqué says five generals called on King Savang Vatthana to report that “the High Command has deemed it has achieved its task of restoring Constitutional legality in order and security.”“Laos King Urged to Act,” New York Times, Jan. 7, 1960, at 4. Check: the day. Names: Savang Vatthana.⟨⟨ Laos ⟩⟩□
  2. In Laos · Laos, By Jan. 6Laotian officials say more than 500 Laotian youths have been kidnapped from their villages in south Laos by rebels, to be trained in North Vietnamese camps.“Reds Said to Seize Laotians,” New York Times, Jan. 7, 1960. Check: the day.⟨⟨ Laos ⟩⟩□

Sunday, Apr. 24
  1. About Laos · Laos, Apr. 24–26Laos elects its Assembly. The CDNI and the government’s candidates sweep; no Neo Lao Hak Xat candidate near a seat. Reports of the Army rigging the count in districts. State, Apr. 26, concerned at “indications elections have been so rigged as to invalidate them in eyes of world opinion.”FRUS 1958–60, XVI, docs. 334, 336, 337, 338 (Dulles to the NSC, Apr. 28). Guan, Vietnamese Communists’ Relations with China and the Second Indochina Conflict, 1956–1962, at 138–139 (an RLG landslide; the election rigged, it seems with CIA agents’ help; at Sam Neua the NLHX candidate 13 votes, the RLG’s 6,508). To check: Arthur J. Dommen, Conflict in Laos: The Politics of Neutralization 129–133 (1964) (cited by Guan, Vietnamese Communists’ Relations with China and the Second Indochina Conflict, 1956–1962, at 139 n.23); Bernard B. Monday, May 23

  3. In Laos · Laos, Sept. 6Vientiane. Souvanna Phouma, Premier, declares that Maj. Gen. Phoumi Nosavan will be considered a rebel if he does not end his resistance to the new regime and return to Vientiane. Souvanna says in an interview that he sent Phoumi a telegram Sept. 5 ordering him to return; it set no deadline.Jacques Nevard, “Resistance Head Warned in Laos,” New York Times, Sept. 7, 1960. About Laos · China: Mao Zedong: Foreign guests · Laos · Vietnam: Diplomacy · China: Foreign affairs, Dec. 17Peking · 5 p.m.The Qinzheng Hall.1 Mao receives Prince Sihanouk, Cambodia’s head of state, his wife and Penn Nouth, Prime Minister, at dinner;2 Liu Shaoqi, Zhu De, Zhou Enlai, Peng Zhen, Chen Yi and others present.3 In his absence Laos has changed: Phoumi, backed by America, its guns and officers, has taken most of Vientiane; Laos now America’s question, not Britain’s or France’s.4 Per the Chinese record, Mao passes on Hồ Chí Minh’s greetings, his invitation to visit the DRV and his request for diplomatic relations; Sihanouk cannot go now, returning to Phnom Penh Dec. 26, and keeps no relations with a divided country, offering consulates instead, as in New Delhi.5

Monday, Dec. 19
  1. About Laos · China · Laos, Dec. 19Peking · eveningThe Chinese government again issues a statement on Laos: the U.S.-backed rebel clique’s large-scale civil war gravely threatens peace in Asia and the world and China’s security. All peace-loving states and peoples should oppose and stop this fanning of the flames.1 China backs the Vietnamese government’s proposal to convene the Geneva conference of the states concerned to stop U.S. aggression.2

  1. About Laos · Laos · Soviet Union, Dec. 20Abramov and the last of Souvanna Phouma’s ministers leave Vientiane.   1. In Laos · Laos, Dec. 21Over Vang Vieng. Lieutenant Colonel Butler Toland, the air attaché in Saigon, in his VC-47 within a hundred feet of a Soviet Il-14 dropping supplies, photographs it with a hand-held camera, fifteen minutes in its pattern. About Laos · China · Laos, Dec. 28Chen Yi writes to the Geneva conference’s co-chairmen, Gromyko, the Soviet Foreign Minister, and Lord Home, the British Foreign Secretary, on the grave situation in Laos: they are asked to take active and effective measures to stop the U.S. government’s wrecking of the Geneva agreement and its interference and aggression in Laos. China bears a responsibility for the security of its own country; the International Commission for Laos should resume work at once and cooperate with Souvanna Phouma’s government to restore peace.Chen Yi nianpu, 850–851 (Dec. 28, 1960; Zeng Yongquan 曾涌泉, Vice Minister, and Song Zhiguang 宋之光, deputy head of the West European Department, hand Chen Yi’s letter, the one to Chervonenko, the other to Rogers (罗杰士), counsellor of the British office of the chargé d’affaires; it asks the co-chairmen to stop the American government’s wrecking of the Geneva agreements and its intervention in Laos); Zhonghua renmin gongheguo waijiao dashiji, II, 179 (Dec. 28, 1960). Boun Oum’s forces against Kong Le and the Pathet Lao, supplied by a Soviet airlift; the French unhelpful, the British coming along. The assembly invests Boun Oum, 41–0 (Check the date).FRUS 1961–63, XXIV, docs. 1, 2. Tuesday, May 16
  1. About Laos · China: Foreign affairs · Laos, May 16Geneva. Chen Yi, head of the Chinese delegation, in his first speech at the enlarged conference on Laos: the Laotian internal question can and must be settled only by the Laotians themselves. The international side of the question is to create the conditions in which the Laotian people can truly do what they wish without outside interference. All states at the conference must share the obligation to ensure Laos’s independence and neutrality. No outside state may use force or threats; none may use aid to wreck Laos’s neutrality. The United States and the states that back its interference must withdraw their military men, and the Kuomintang remnants in Laos must be disarmed and sent out. Only by abolishing the aggressive Southeast Asia military bloc can peace and security be kept in Southeast Asia, Laos included.Chen Yi nianpu, 872–873 (May 16, 1961; Chen Yi’s first speech, after the opening; the 1954 agreements a good base; Laos’s long unrest the work of American interference; its internal questions for the Lao alone; American and other foreign military personnel to leave; the Kuomintang remnants to be disarmed and sent out; only the end of SEATO can keep the peace; Vice-President Johnson’s tour of South Vietnam, Thailand and the Philippines cannot but alert us); Zhonghua renmin gongheguo waijiao dashiji, II, 195–196 (May 16, 1961). Names: Chen Yi.⟨⟨ China: Foreign affairs ⟩⟩⟨⟨ China ⟩⟩⟨⟨ Laos ⟩⟩□

  1. About Laos · Laos, Aug. 29Washington · 11 a.m.The Cabinet Room, 11 a.m., on Southeast Asia: Kennedy with Rusk, McNamara, Robert Kennedy, Harriman, Dulles, Lemnitzer and others;1 Harriman to see Souvanna.2 NSAM 80: the mobile training teams in Laos raised to 500, advisers down to the company; 2,000 more Meo supported, 11,000 in all; photo-reconnaissance over Laos by Thai or sanitized aircraft.3 Lemnitzer, on a force for southern Laos: the first, by Reeves, 13,000.4 Kennedy: no commitment to SEATO Plan 5 “without regard to whatever else may happen in the world.” Lemnitzer: the plan starts with about 13,000 Americans, 4,000 ground combat troops in Laos and nearly 9,000 supporting forces in Thailand. U. Alexis Johnson: an expanded SEATO Plan 5 would go by stages, beginning with a cease-fire along the May 3 line, and would not start without assurances of help from Asian allies. Taylor: the 30,000-odd troop estimate is the initial cost, not the final bill. Rusk: 40,000 troops in Laos would almost all have to be supplied by the United States.5 By McNamara’s memoir, Rusk’s plan is some 30,000 combat troops from the treaty’s signatories, and McNamara argues that with six divisions, about 90,000 men, going to Europe, war in Southeast Asia too is inconceivable short of total mobilization.6

About Laos · Vietnam: Hanoi · China, Oct. 5Zhongnanhai, the Yinian Tang, afternoon.1 Mao Zedong receives a Vietnamese military delegation led by Võ Nguyên Giáp;2 Liu Shaoqi, Zhou Enlai, Zhu De, Deng Xiaoping, Ye Jianying, Luo Ruiqing and Xiao Xiangrong present.3 Mao: imperialism reaches too far, “ten fingers on ten fleas: in the end it catches none”; in South Vietnam and Laos the Vietnamese have caught one of America’s “fingers”; five or ten more years of war, and when they call for a Geneva conference America may have to compromise, or else intervene further; an attack on the North must reckon with the South’s guerrillas, the peoples’ struggles in Laos and Thailand, China, Korea and the North’s own strength; “America does not yet dare move lightly”.4

Only an immediate halt to U.S. aggression and interference in Laos can turn round the present dangerous situation. China fully supports the proposal made on May 5 by Souphanouvong, Deputy Prime Minister of the Lao government of national union and chairman of the Neo Lao Hak Xat, and fully supports the stand in the Vietnamese Foreign Ministry’s statement of May 12.   1. About Laos · China · Laos, Apr. 22The Foreign Ministry issues a statement on the present situation in Laos. The military coup the U.S. and the pro-U.S. Lao clique launched at Vientiane is an open and serious breach of the Geneva agreements, which China cannot look on at. Any wrecking of the Lao government of national union under the coup group’s coercion is illegal. China fully supports the statement of Prince Souphanouvong of Apr. 19 and the just demands in the Vietnamese Foreign Ministry’s statement of Apr. 20. About Laos · China: Foreign affairs · Laos, May 26Chen Yi, Foreign Minister, writes to the two co-chairmen of the Geneva conference and the participants, proposing a conference of the foreign ministers of 14 states at Geneva in June, to discuss Laos first. The Lao situation, he says, is getting more serious by the day. U.S. aircraft’s bombing and reconnaissance flights in Laos are the first step of direct armed interference; at the same time the U.S. and its followers have stepped up attacks and aggression against Cambodia and publicly plot to widen the war of aggression in South Vietnam, so that the peace and security of the whole Indochina region are gravely threatened. He hopes the co-chairmen will bring the three Lao sides together to form a delegation of the three forces to attend, so that the conference may meet soon.Chen Yi nianpu, 1031 (May 26, 1964); Zhonghua renmin gongheguo waijiao dashiji, II, 338–339 (May 26, 1964). Mao to Sangsiv, head of the Neo Lao Hak Sat’s cultural group, Lian Guan of the National People’s Congress Standing Committee present. The mass line: the cultural group and the army to dress, eat and labor as the masses do, with the Three Disciplines and Eight Attentions; the Chinese Party’s mistakes, two right and three left; bourgeois intellectuals under a new rectification campaign; capitalism restored in the Soviet Union under Khrushchev.Mao Zedong with Sangsiv, Beijing, Sept. 4, 1964, doc. 1, 77 Conversations Between Chinese and Foreign Leaders on the Indochina War, 1964–1977 (Odd Arne Westad, ed., 1998) (online), 66–69 (excerpts, the editors’ ellipses kept; 66 nn.108–109 gloss the Front and Lian Guan, 68 n.110 Aidit). Monday, Sept. 7
  1. About Laos · Vietnam: Air war · Laos, Sept. 7Washington, the principals without the President. Wheeler presents a JCS proposal for “deliberately provocative actions” against North Vietnam, then a systematic bombing campaign of increasing severity. Taylor opposes it; the others agree. Systematic bombing might be needed “depending on GVN progress and Communist reaction in the meantime,” but not yet. They will recommend to Johnson limited actions to “show the Communists we mean business”: naval patrols in the Tonkin Gulf and Oplan 34-A operations resumed, consultations with Souvanna Phouma for limited South Vietnamese operations in Laos, preparations “to respond on a tit-for-tat basis” to provocations.Fredrik Logevall, Choosing War: The Lost Chance for Peace and the Escalation of War in Vietnam 233–34 (1999) (the meeting of Sept. 7; the proposal, Taylor, the agreement, the actions). To check: William Bundy’s summary of the meeting, attached to McGeorge Bundy to Johnson, Sept. 8, 1964, FRUS 1964–68, I, doc. 342 (cited by Logevall, Choosing War, 234 n.23). See Sept. 6. About Laos · China: Foreign affairs · Laos · Vietnam: Hanoi, Dec. 31Chen Yi, Vice-Premier and Foreign Minister, cables Prince Souphanouvong, Deputy Prime Minister of Laos, and Xuân Thủy, Foreign Minister of the DRV. China supports the Lao and Vietnamese peoples’ just struggle and condemns the U.S. for widening the war of aggression from South Vietnam to Laos. It entirely agrees with Souphanouvong’s proposal to convene a conference of the 14 states party to the Geneva agreement, to seek a peaceful settlement of the Lao question. He hopes the two co-chairmen of the Geneva conference will take on the duty of upholding the Geneva agreement and the peace of Indochina, and take the necessary measures to stop the U.S. widening of the war in Indochina.Chen Yi nianpu, 1076–1077 (Dec. 31, 1964; the reply to Xuân Thủy’s letter of Dec. 21, and the cable to Souphanouvong on his statement of Dec. 17); Zhonghua renmin gongheguo waijiao dashiji, II, 378 (Dec. 31, 1964). April 1969

Apr., late–June
  1. In Laos · Laos · Vietnam: Hanoi, Apr., late–JuneLaos. Vang Pao’s special forces and the right-wing army, directed by the Americans, open three operations, Samakkhi (Solidarity) I, II and III, to take Xieng Khoảng town and the ground round the Plain of Jars. The Lao People’s Liberation Army’s 1st and 701st Battalions, with the local forces and guerrillas of Mường Khun, stop and wear them down, and they fall back to Sam Thong and Long Tieng.Viện Lịch sử quân sự Việt Nam, Lịch sử kháng chiến chống Mỹ, cứu nước (1954–1975), VI, 239. June 1969

Thursday, June 19
  1. About Laos · Vietnam: Hanoi · Laos, June 19The Politburo’s resolution no. 190-NQ/TW on helping “Party X,” the Lao People’s Revolutionary Party, build the economy and culture of its liberated zone, run since 1965 on the scale of a state: the aid plans ill fitted to Hanoi’s budget, the advisers too few, transport of goods poor. The three-year plan of aid, 1968–70, to be pressed, a new plan prepared for a lull; the aid organization at home strengthened.Nghị quyết của Bộ Chính trị số 190-NQ/TW, ngày 19 tháng 6 năm 1969, Về việc giúp Đảng X đẩy mạnh xây dựng kinh tế, phát triển văn hóa ở vùng giải phóng, signed for the Politburo by Nguyễn Duy Trinh; “Đảng X,” the editors’ note (212 n.). Văn kiện Đảng toàn tập, XXX, 212–18. Made public: 2004.⟨⟨ Vietnam: Hanoi ⟩⟩⟨⟨ Vietnam ⟩⟩⟨⟨ Laos ⟩⟩□
Monday, June 23
  1. In Laos · Vietnam: Hanoi · Laos, June 23–24Muong Soui · nightLaos, the night of June 23–24: Vietnamese and Lao forces open the Mường Sủi (Muong Soui) campaign against Vang Pao’s mobile forces, to hold the Plain of Jars and threaten Sam Thong and Long Tieng. On the Vietnamese side the 316th Division less a part, three sapper battalions, two of 120-mm mortars, two of 12.7-mm antiaircraft guns, two tank companies; on the Lao, two infantry battalions and others. By 6 a.m. June 24 the Muong Soui airfield under their guns; June 28 to July 1 the whole of Muong Soui taken.Viện Lịch sử quân sự Việt Nam, Lịch sử kháng chiến chống Mỹ, cứu nước (1954–1975), VI, 239–40. Saturday, June 28
  1. In Laos · Laos · Vietnam: Hanoi, June 28–July 1Mường Sủi. The Vietnamese and Lao forces take all of Mường Sủi and pursue the remnants to the Salaphu Khun junction, threatening Sam Thong and Long Tieng; the campaign ends. By their count the long-held defenses are broken. Khamtay Siphandone says it shows the Lao–Vietnamese forces can beat the “intensified special war”; UPI, June 28, calls it the Americans’ costliest battle in Laos since the start of 1969.Viện Lịch sử quân sự Việt Nam, Lịch sử kháng chiến chống Mỹ, cứu nước (1954–1975), VI, 240 and n. 1. July 1969

Thursday, July 31
  1. In Laos · Laos · Vietnam: Hanoi, July 31Laos. Under cover of American air and artillery, a mixed force from Sam Thong–Long Tieng and Vang Vieng, Vang Pao’s men, the right-wing army and 5,000 Thais, 18 battalions and 52 companies of special forces in all, opens Kou Kiet and drives into the center of the Plain of Jars. The rains have flooded the defenders’ works; the advance is fast, with villages burned.Viện Lịch sử quân sự Việt Nam, Lịch sử kháng chiến chống Mỹ, cứu nước (1954–1975), VI, 241–42 and n. 1. September 1969

Late September
  1. In Laos · Laos · Vietnam: Hanoi, Sept., lateLaos. By September the Americans and their allies hold the Plain of Jars and stand at the gates near the Vietnamese border, Bản Ban and Nong Het. At the end of the month the Vietnamese troops are ordered back to rest and refit, leaving a little over a battalion with the Lao to hold a springboard; the Lao and Vietnamese decide on a counteroffensive, Campaign 139.Viện Lịch sử quân sự Việt Nam, Lịch sử kháng chiến chống Mỹ, cứu nước (1954–1975), VI, 242–43. See Oct. 25. Check: the days; the history gives the month and “cuối tháng 9-1969”.⟨⟨ Laos ⟩⟩⟨⟨ Vietnam: Hanoi ⟩⟩⟨⟨ Vietnam ⟩⟩□

October 1969

Saturday, Oct. 25
  1. In Laos · Vietnam: Hanoi · Laos, Oct. 25Laos. Vietnamese and Lao forces open Campaign 139, the counteroffensive for the Plain of Jars and Xieng Khouang, Vang Pao’s Kou Kiet having taken the plain by September: its first phase, to build up the position, through the rains and the bombing. On the Vietnamese side the 312th and 316th Divisions, two battalions of the 866th Regiment, the 16th Artillery and the 45th Engineer Regiments, a tank company and the 20th, 25A and 25B Sapper Battalions; on the Lao, ten infantry battalions and others. Vũ Lập commander, Huỳnh Đắc Hương political commissar. The campaign runs to Apr. 25, 1970: 6,668 of the enemy put out of action and the plain retaken, by its count.Viện Lịch sử quân sự Việt Nam, Lịch sử kháng chiến chống Mỹ, cứu nước (1954–1975), VI, 241–46. Names: Vang Pao, Vũ Lập, Huỳnh Đắc Hương.⟨⟨ Vietnam: Hanoi ⟩⟩⟨⟨ Vietnam ⟩⟩⟨⟨ Laos ⟩⟩□
